newsitem.title: UK: Severn Trent criticised over prices.
newsitem.headline: Severn Trent criticised over prices.

text.p: Severn Trent Plc, one of Britain's top 10 water and sewage companies, was accused on Monday of having short-changed consumers in an open letter from a customer lobby group.

Water industry watchdog Ofwat's Customer Service Committee (CSC) said the monopoly water supplier had put shareholders before customers by raising prices too sharply, while splashing out on robust dividends and fat executive wage packages.

In a letter to Severn Trent's managing director Brian Duckworth, CSC chairman Clive Wilkinson said the company's share price, trading at a new year high of 747p on Monday, had more than tripled, while customer bills had risen by 78 percent since privatisation in 1989.
Customers had also suffered two hosepipe bans and 'severe disruption' of services during the 1995 drought, he added.

'...the service delivered to customers and the capital investment over six years could well have been delivered at a substantially lower cost to customers if Severn Trent had chosen to do so,' Wilkinson said.
The CSC has asked Severn Trent to limit a regulated annual increase in customer bills to 3.2 percent above inflation.
Severn Trent, which raised its half year dividend by 14 percent last November, lifted average household prices by 4.2 percent above inflation.
But Wilkinson, who has launched a regular attack on the water company, did concede that the company's service record had improved since privatisation.

Ofwat director general Ian Byatt is setting fresh limits on water companies' bills for the year 2000 and Wilkinson said he would be pressing to ensure substantial price cuts, in real terms, to see customers get a 'fair share' of efficiency benefits.
